# Themis Review Remediation Register

2026-10-09 · Sebastian Hansson

The external review of 2026-10-09 holds up: of its 33 findings, 28 are confirmed against the current documents, 4 are partly right and 1 overreaches. None of them breaks a principle or an invariant. Ten findings touch milestone 1, and six of those need your decision before the coder builds the posting path (RR-01 to RR-06). RR-11 also needs a decision before the Item table is built. The rest are scheduled against the phase they block.

**Status 2026-10-09:** you accepted RR-01 to RR-06, RR-08, RR-11, RR-19 and RR-22, with three adjustments: R-MD-05 cites the scope on each attribute instead of listing scopes; the lock order table lists StockBalance from milestone 1; costing method sits on ItemCompany, not the ItemCostState cache. They are recorded as R-MD-05, D-43, D-44 and amendments to D-22, D-37, D-41 and R-LED-08, and an independent review of the edits has been applied. The afternoon review added RR-34 to RR-38, all accepted, and moved the event envelope part of RR-15 forward to before Phase 1.

Each row below cites what the review said, what the documents actually say, my proposed resolution, and which rule or decision it would change. Nothing marked as a proposal has been applied. The Decision column is yours: set it to Accept, Reject or Changed, or comment on the row.

Basis: Themis Foundation Design rev 100, Themis Phase 0 Specification rev 117, Themis Build Brief rev 22. Review IDs (RR-xx) are local to this register; accepted items become rules (R-xx) or decisions (D-xx) in the foundation decision log.

## Milestone 1: decide now

RR-01 to RR-06 sit on the posting path the coder builds next; each is small and each needs your call because it changes a rule or decision text. RR-07 to RR-10 are cheap to settle now and expensive to retrofit.

| ID | Finding | What the documents say | Proposed resolution | Changes | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RR-01 | Duplicate item number has no rule ID | Spec: `item_number` "Unique per installation". R-API-03 requires a rule ID on every rejection, and the brief's checklist expects one | New rule R-MD-05: business keys (item number, company code and the like) are unique within their stated scope; a duplicate is rejected with R-MD-05. Invariant | New rule | [Accept] |
| RR-02 | D-37 says "never as JSON numbers" but its note accepts numbers inbound | Both texts are in the foundation; you confirmed the inbound tolerance on 2026-10-08 | Reword D-37: responses and events carry money and quantities as JSON strings, never numbers; requests accept strings or numbers and parse the number text exactly, never through a binary float | D-37 wording | [Accept] |
| RR-03 | Average cost is "never rounded" yet stored as numeric(28,10) | Spec step 6 says never rounded; the brief's TEST-003 stores 0.0166666667. Step 2 (inbound without entered cost) multiplies by the stored average even while stock is above 0 | Step 6: stored average_cost is value / quantity rounded half away from zero to 10 decimals. Step 2: while quantity is above 0, cost = q x value / quantity computed exactly, then rounded to the minor unit; the stored average is used only when quantity is 0 | Spec costing steps 2 and 6 (R-INV-05) | [Accept] |
| RR-04 | Every state change must emit an outbox event, but the catalogue names only posting events | Brief: "Every state change writes its outbox event". Spec names events for document transitions only; nothing for ITEM.CREATE or adjustment CREATE, UPDATE, DISCARD | Naming convention instead of a hand-written catalogue: TYPE plus past tense, version 1, payload = id plus changed fields (ITEM_CREATED, INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT_CREATED, _UPDATED, _DISCARDED; INVENTORY_ADJUSTED for POST already exists). Business payloads are specified only for events that integrations consume | Spec events section; brief conventions row | [Accept] |
| RR-05 | Lock order covers only part of what a posting locks (partly right) | R-LED-08: cost state rows by item id, then number series. The M1 posting also writes the document row and StockBalance. Because every StockBalance row written belongs to an item whose cost-state lock is already held, M1 cannot deadlock if all cost-state locks are taken first in one statement, as the brief says. Reservations and allocation in Phase 1 are not covered | Restate R-LED-08 as the full order: the command's own document row, cost state rows by item id, stock balance rows in key order, reservations and source lines by id (Phase 1), number series last. Add an M1 concurrency test: two adjustments on the same items in opposite line order | R-LED-08 (invariant) | [Accept] |
| RR-06 | "No retrying execution strategy" leaves serialization failures and deadlock victims unhandled | D-41 and R-DB-01 forbid statement-level retries, correctly, because a retry would replay half a command | Allow a bounded retry of the whole command in a new transaction, at most 3 attempts, only for SQLSTATE 40001 and 40P01. Safe because the idempotency record commits in the same transaction | D-41 amendment | [Accept] |
| RR-07 | No command traceability matrix | Permissions, If-Match, idempotency, events and rule IDs are stated as conventions, not per command | A machine-readable command catalogue in the repository (command, permission, If-Match, transition, audit, event, rule IDs, error codes, tests), starting with the 5 M1 commands. A CI check fails when a command lacks a test citing its rules | Brief conventions | [Pending] |
| RR-08 | Repository snapshots drift from the planning documents | Confirmed in practice today: the coder never received the brief, and the snapshots already lag the source. Your project instructions make the planning documents the source of truth | Keep the planning documents canonical while the design is moving. Every snapshot header carries the source doc rev and date; refreshing snapshots becomes part of every change that touches the build. A doc-lint CI job checks that every rule ID cited in code and tests exists in the snapshots. Revisit making the repository canonical when Phase 1 starts | Brief; changing the canonical source would change your project instructions | [Accept] |
| RR-09 | No secure delivery baseline | Only the licence scan and secrets handling are defined | Turn on now in GitHub: Dependabot security alerts, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL for C#. Before going public: SBOM, signed releases, a security policy and vulnerability disclosure. Owner decision 2026-10-17 (Changed): Dependabot security alerts stay on. Secret scanning with push protection and CodeQL are not used while the repository is private, because they need paid GitHub licences there; the owner removed the secret scanning rule from the main ruleset. Revisit when the repository goes public (D-14, D-36), where they are free. Until then secrets stay out of the repository by design: real secret values are handled by the owner outside any LLM or agent harness, and the build only ever sees placeholders (Build Brief Secrets row), so a scanner would have nothing real to find. The before-going-public items stand. Owner decision 2026-10-18 (Changed): the repository is public, with secret scanning, push protection, CodeQL default setup (C# and Actions) and private vulnerability reporting switched on by the owner (checked 2026-10-19). The SBOM and signed releases move to the first release, since there is no release yet. A SECURITY.md security policy is still to be added to the repository | Brief stack row | [Changed] |
| RR-10 | "Contract-first with OpenAPI" versus OpenAPI generated from code | Foundation API row says contract-first; the brief uses ASP.NET Core built-in generation, which is code-first | Code-first generation, with the generated OpenAPI document committed to the repository and a CI diff that fails on breaking changes unless the pull request is labelled as breaking | Foundation API row (Proposed status) | [Pending] |

| RR-12 | P-11 requires settings tables, but no settings model exists | No Setting entity in the spec; M1 uses the company's tax rounding level as a plain column | Specify a settings framework: setting definition (key, value type, documented default, validation), the scope levels it may be overridden at (installation, company, site, warehouse), effective dating where history matters, and audit. First known consumer: the 7-day idempotency retention, a code constant under the temporary exception D-45 until this exists | New spec section | [Pending] |
| RR-13 | Company isolation is incomplete | Row-level security is planned after M1; how reporting views respect it is explicitly undecided | Before a second company's data exists: how company context enters the transaction, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, which roles may bypass it, owner-rights views versus security-barrier views, BI identities, and tests for cross-company reads as well as writes | Spec security section | [Pending] |
| RR-14 | Insert-only audit conflicts with erasure | R-MD-03 anonymises personal data, but audit events hold before and after values and are insert-only | Audit stores a reference instead of the value for fields classified as personal data; the values live in an erasable table that anonymisation clears. Simpler than encryption-key destruction and needs no reader-side overlay | R-MD-03 detail; audit entity | [Pending] |
| RR-15 | Outbox delivery semantics are undefined | Outbox table and relay exist; ordering, claiming, retries, dead letters and retention are not specified | Envelope first, before Phase 1 (your decision 2026-10-09): event id, type and schema version (D-44), aggregate id, occurred at, company, and whether correlation id, command name and idempotency key travel with it; kernel.outbox_event has no correlation id today, so adding one is a small migration now and costly once consumers exist. Then, before integrations, specify: per-aggregate ordering, claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, retry with backoff and a dead-letter state, retention period, and the rule that payloads carry no personal data beyond ids. Owner decision 2026-10-17 (Changed): the envelope is decided as D-50 and built in milestone 1 step 7 (aggregate type, company, command name, correlation id; no idempotency key, no user). Add natural duplicate controls where an external reference exists (supplier invoice number per supplier, bank transaction id per account). Posting is already protected by the state machine: a Posted document cannot be posted again | R-API-01 note; spec | [Pending] |
| RR-17 | Scenario catalogue unwritten | Spec lists it as "to write next" | Already the next design step. Write it before Phase 0 is declared complete | None | [Pending] |

## Where the review overreaches

One finding argues against a position the documents do not take (RR-32); another repeats a limit the documents already state (RR-33, partly right).

| ID | Review says | What the documents actually say | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| RR-32 | Phases 0 to 2 are treated as build-ready through a first financial close, which the missing purchasing and close specifications contradict | D-30 sets the build order and the next steps list the Phase 1 purchasing and Phase 2 finance specifications as still to write. Only milestone 1 has a build brief. Nothing claims Phases 1 and 2 are ready | Overreach. The useful part, that kernel confidence must not outrun the specifications, is covered by RR-17, RR-20 and RR-25 |
| RR-33 | Database role switching limits the security boundary | D-41 and the brief already say the role model stops mistakes, not malicious code in the application process, and name security-definer ledger inserts as the later option | Partly right. Nothing new, except one addition worth keeping: an allow-list of which role each command may switch to, checked by the pipeline. Fold into the D-41 follow-up when row-level security is designed (RR-13) |

The review's overall verdict matches the plan: build milestone 1 as an architecture experiment, use it to challenge the design, and validate procure-to-pay and real workflows before the kernel is frozen. Its main warning, that a convincing kernel can create premature confidence, is the reason RR-20 and RR-22 sit before the Phase 1 freeze.
